title: Some Thoughts on LotR: Journeys in Middle Earth
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rAxPIoC8bB4

Not a review, Daniel (@dungeondive) stresses, but preliminary thoughts on Lord of the Rings: Journeys in Middle-earth. He shelved it after early plays when the scenario time limits irked his group, then came back once the adventure mode removed the clock and the Shadowed Paths expansion added enemy variety. He's now mid-campaign with Gandalf as a Meddler and a second hero as a Traveler.

Much of the video is a spirited defence of app-driven games. Letting the app handle enemy AI, encounters and number-crunch frees him to focus on the adventure itself, and he has little patience for "the app won't exist in ten years": that's like refusing a great bottle of scotch because someday it will be gone. Bugs can be patched without reprinting anything. He'd love a Runebound with this kind of app.

The licence is a harder sell. He loves The Hobbit as a book but not The Lord of the Rings, and loves the films but not the Hobbit films. Meanwhile Tolkien purists find the game not Lord of the Rings enough, so it sits in an awkward middle ground. His biggest gripe is the sheer number of map tiles: hunting through oddly shaped terrain stalls the game, as it does in Mansions of Madness. He'd rather expansions lived in the app. Still, as an app-based adventure game it scratches the itch.

----

Where do you stand on app-driven board games: worth enjoying now, or a risk you won't take on a game's long-term future?
